review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–185) and checked it only against the simp-interface rubric. The file has no @[simp] attributes, no custom simp sets, and no simp-normal-form claims. Simp is used only in small, local ways: `simp [ψ₁, ψ₂, G]`, `simp` for `hblk`, and `simp only [map_smul, coeff_wS_single, smul_eq_mul]` and `simp only [GM, ← coe_substAlgHom …, map_sum, map_smul, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← smul_add]`. The two `simp only` calls name every rule they use, so they don't depend on the global simp set. The reversed `← coe_substAlgHom` rewrites are restricted to the `simp only` call and are undone by an explicit `rw` afterwards. I saw no cycle risk and no competing rules in that call. The lemmas `coeff_wS`, `coeff_wS_single`, `coeff_wS_of_ne` and `subst_coe_coe` could be tagged simp. I did not recommend that. Each is used only once or twice, and `coeff_wS_single` has an `if` on a sum condition. Tagging them would only add simp annotations for identities that look simple, which the rubric tells me not to do. I did not run Lean, so I can't say anything about the actual simp behaviour beyond what the source shows. I found no justified simp-interface problem.
